name: Sela Tunnel
facts: Sela Tunnel, the world’s longest bi‑lane tunnel, stretches 1,555 metres at 3,000 metres elevation, cutting through the Sela–Chabrela ridge to keep the 171‑km Bomdila‑Tawang road open all year.

Launched in February 2019, the tunnel’s twin tubes were excavated simultaneously, finishing the escape tube in July 2021 and allowing the entire project to open in March 2024, just in time for Prime Minister Modi’s dedication.
Named after Monpa heroine Sela, the tunnel honors her 72‑hour stand against Chinese forces in 1962, a sacrifice commemorated by nearby Jaswant Garh and Nuranang Falls memorials.
